title: Findings and Follow-up Actions on National Service Training Death
what_it_is: Findings and Follow-up Actions on National Service Training Death

sections.label: COI preliminary findings to Armed Forces Council
sections.summary: The COI submitted preliminary findings to the Armed Forces Council on 16 July, and the House is updated on findings and SAF follow-up actions since May.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: The COI has submitted its preliminary findings to the Armed Forces Council on 16 July this year and I would like to update this House on their findings, as well as follow-up actions taken by the Singapore Armed Forces (SAF) since May.

sections.label: COI finds training breaches
sections.summary: The COI found Combat Circuit 4 training compliant, but found breaches of Training Safety Regulations for Cardiovascular 6 and of an Army directive for a later event.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: The COI found the training for Combat Circuit 4 to be compliant with regulations or guidelines.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: However, the COI did discover breaches of the Army's Training Safety Regulations (TSR) for Cardiovascular 6 and breaches of the Army's directive for another subsequent event that took place later that day.

sections.label: Reduced rest timing between laps
sections.summary: The rest timing between each lap was reduced to one minute, 45 seconds shorter than the lesson plan stipulated.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: The rest timing in between each lap was noted to be reduced to one minute, which is 45 seconds shorter than what was stipulated in the lesson plan.

sections.label: Unauthorised collective punishment before fast march
sections.summary: The collective punishment meted out to CFC Lee's platoon before the next day's fast march was not authorised.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Later that night, before the fast march the next day, the collective punishment that was meted out to CFC Lee's platoon was also not authorised.

sections.label: Unauthorised punishment compromised rest
sections.summary: The COI found unauthorised informal punishment compromised the seven hours of uninterrupted rest, leaving trainees about six hours 15 minutes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: The COI found that the conduct of unauthorised informal punishment compromised the seven hours of uninterrupted rest as the trainees had about six hours 15 minutes instead.

sections.label: CFC Lee's eight-km fast march
sections.summary: CFC Lee was the last to complete the eight-km fast march in around 100 minutes, including the 20-minute break.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: CFC Lee was the last one to complete the eight-km fast march in around 100 minutes, including the 20-minute break.

sections.label: First aid and cooling measures
sections.summary: First aid given included removing equipment, unbuttoning uniform, ice packs, water; the COI found onsite cooling inadequate, including no IV drip.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: The first aid that was administered comprised the removal of CFC Lee’s equipment, unbuttoning his uniform, applying ice packs at his vital points, pouring water on him and giving him water.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: However, the COI noted that the onsite cooling measures administered were inadequate, including the failure to administer an onsite intravenous (IV) drip, the improper placement of ice packs and the improper use of a ground sheet.

sections.label: CFC Lee's death
sections.summary: His condition deteriorated and he passed away on 30 April 2018.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: Unfortunately, his condition deteriorated and he passed away on 30 April 2018.

sections.label: COI findings on heat stroke
sections.summary: The COI found death resulted from heat stroke causing multiple organ injury, with likely reasons being inadequate onsite casualty management and delayed evacuation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: The COI found that CFC Lee’s death was the result of heat stroke leading to multiple organ injury.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: While the COI was unable to ascertain the direct causes which led CFC Lee to suffer from his heat stroke, it noted that possible contributing causes were accumulated fatigue, insufficient rest, CFC Lee’s less than optimal state of health and his potential use of medication.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: However, the COI’s preliminary assessment was that the likely reasons for CFC Lee succumbing to the heat stroke were inadequate onsite casualty management and delayed evacuation to the medical centre.

sections.label: Relevant persons removed from command
sections.summary: The relevant persons in this incident had been removed from command.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Defence (Dr Ng Eng Hen)
sentences.text: In the meantime, the relevant persons in this incident had been removed from command.

sections.label: Simplified evacuation protocol
sections.summary: A simplified protocol will have all SAF commanders and medics evacuate every trainee who cannot answer simple questions on time, place and identity.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: First, a simplified protocol to lower the bar for immediate evacuation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Under this protocol, all commanders and medics across the SAF will evacuate every trainee that cannot respond to simple questions on time, place and identity.

sections.label: Arm Immersion Cooling System
sections.summary: The Army will implement the Arm Immersion Cooling System, used in US and Australian militaries, for fast marches and route marches of 12 km and longer.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: For example, the Army will implement what is called the Arm Immersion Cooling System – you immerse your arms – and this has been used in the United States (US) and Australian militaries to reduce heat injury for all fast marches and route marches that are 12 km and longer.

sections.label: Safety lesson plans and tests
sections.summary: Lesson plans on safety will be improved and the annual Training Safety Regulation test will include mandatory heat injury questions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: Lesson plans on safety will be improved and the annual Training Safety Regulation test will also include mandatory questions on heat injury prevention and management.

sections.label: SAF updates COI findings
sections.summary: The SAF has updated the family of the COI's findings and the actions it is taking to prevent recurrences of the lapses found.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The SAF has updated the family of the COI’s findings and the actions that the SAF is taking to prevent recurrences of the lapses found.

sections.label: Three troopers as marshals
sections.summary: The COI recounted findings that three troopers did not fulfil all conducting officer conditions and were deployed as marshals, not on the fast march.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The findings were recounted by the COI and that three troopers stood out, declared that they did not fulfil all the conditions of the conducting officer, and they were deployed as marshals and were not put on the eight-km fast march.

sections.label: Immediate training safety regulation
sections.summary: The immediate training safety regulation is that anyone disoriented is taken out and sent to the medical centre.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The immediate training safety regulation, effective now, is that we do not really care what the reason is.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: As soon as anybody is disoriented, we take him out, we send him to the medical centre, where there are facilities, where there is expertise.

sections.label: Heat injury evacuation and work-rest cycles
sections.summary: A person not oriented to time, place or identity is evacuated, and wet globe temperature sensors mandate work-rest cycles rather than commander discretion.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: If he is not oriented to time, place and identity – that is, to either one, not all three – you evacuate him.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But in the face of global warming – and the last few months have been very, very intense weather – I am just curious: are commanders given the discretion to, in extreme weather conditions, extreme heat waves, pare down the training, or is there a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) to allow them to have flexibility, not during normal times, but extreme heat situations?

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: It is not discretionary, and Members will remember when I updated this House about what the requirements are for fast marches or any training activities, we use special sensors which measure the wet globe temperature and, depending on what the temperature is based on this instrument, you mandate work-rest cycles – you can only work so much and you need to rest so much.

sections.label: COI findings on CFC Lee
sections.summary: The COI found CFC Dave Lee's death resulted from heat stroke, with possible contributory causes and likely reasons of inadequate casualty management and delayed evacuation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: And they started from the day before the fast march.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: I have related how there were a number of activities, two of which did not comply with Training Safety Regulations – one part of the lesson plan where CFC Lee ran faster than he should have for three laps of 400 metres each.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: And that night where there was an informal unauthorised punishment which lasted 30-35 minutes which resulted in them not having seven hours of sleep as required – they had about six hours 15 minutes or thereabouts.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The COI concluded, based on all these findings – and I would repeat this because I think it is important – that CFC Dave Lee's death was a result of heat stroke.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: The COI was unable to ascertain the direct causes which led CFC Lee to suffer from heat stroke.

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: It noted the possible contributory causes were "accumulated fatigue, insufficient rest and less than optimal state of health and his potential use of medication".

sentences.speaker: Dr Ng Eng Hen
sentences.text: But their preliminary assessment was that the likely reasons for him succumbing to the heat stroke were inadequate onsite casualty management and delayed evacuation to the medical centre.
